cv_guide.meta_title: How to write a good CV: 8 keys
cv_guide.meta_description: Practical guide to a CV that makes sense in 5 seconds: headline, summary, achievements with numbers, design, education, languages and more. With examples.
cv_guide.title: How to write a good CV
cv_guide.intro: A recruiter spends a few seconds on each CV. These 8 keys work for almost any job and country: use them as a checklist.
cv_guide.cta_text: The CoverCraft CV builder is free: clean templates, PDF download and an ATS-friendly version.

headline.title: 1. A headline with the exact job
headline.why: It is the first thing read after your name. It should say which job you want, not everything you can do.
how: One headline per type of job: if you are after two kinds of jobs, make two CVs.
Add at most 2 or 3 key specialties or tools.

summary.title: 2. A summary you can read in 5 seconds
summary.why: The summary explains why you fit. If it tells a long story, nobody reaches the end.
how: Formula: what you are + your strongest experience + your specialty + what you are looking for.
2 to 4 sentences. No clichés like "proactive" or "team player" unless you prove them.
summary.bad: Ever since I was a child I have been passionate about technology and new challenges…
summary.good: Technician with 6 years in production-line maintenance. Specialised in PLC and pneumatics. Looking for a preventive maintenance role in a plant.

titles.title: 3. Job titles people understand in that country
titles.why: Each country names the same jobs differently. If the recruiter does not recognise your title, they do not know what you did.
how: Use the local equivalent of your title, without inflating it.
Never use a title you did not have; if needed, explain the role in the first line.
titles.bad: "Residente de obra" (in a CV for the UK)

design.title: 4. A clean, easy-to-read design
design.why: Design should help reading, not grab attention. Many applicant tracking systems (ATS) do not read columns and graphics well.
how: Readable font, clean margins and clear sections. One page if you have under 10 years of experience.
Photos depend on the country: common in Spain and Mexico, not used in the US or the UK.
Also send an ATS version (one column, real text) when the company uses a job portal.
design.bad: Skill-level bars, icons everywhere, coloured backgrounds
design.good: One or two clean columns, a single accent colour

metrics.title: 5. Achievements with numbers, not duties
metrics.why: "Responsible for…" says what you were supposed to do; an achievement says what you got done.
how: Formula: verb + what you did + measurable result (people, money, time, %).
If you do not have the exact figure, use an honest estimate ("about 40 people"). Never make it up.
metrics.good: Handled 100+ material requisitions and reduced supply stoppages

relevance.title: 6. Most relevant first
relevance.why: The recruiter looks for what the job asks for. If it is on page two, it does not exist.
how: Order sections and achievements for the job: the best fit goes on top.
If your company is not known in that country, add one line of context: sector, size or clients.
relevance.bad: Construcciones Norte S.A. de C.V. (nothing else)
relevance.good: Construcciones Norte: industrial construction company in northern Mexico, about 300 employees

education.title: 7. Education and courses that add value
education.why: Every line that adds nothing takes attention away from the ones that do.
how: Highest degree first. Leave out secondary school if you have a degree.
Only courses related to the job.
If the job requires an official degree, say whether it is recognised or in progress.
education.bad: Ten online courses on unrelated topics
education.good: Master's in Business Analytics and AI · top of the class

languages.title: 8. Languages and tools with a real level
languages.why: "English: high" says nothing. A level and some proof do.
how: Real level (A1 to C2, or native) and, if possible, proof: a certificate or an example of use.
Tools used in that country; if yours is little known, add its equivalent.
languages.good: English B2 (presented a project to the client in English) · OPUS (similar to Presto)
